title: Ubuntu
description: Debian-based distribution by Canonical. The most widely used Linux distro for servers and cloud. LTS releases get 5 years of support.

breakdown.meaning: Advanced Package Tool — Ubuntu/Debian package manager
Assume yes — skip interactive confirmation prompt

flags.description: Remove package and its config files

example: apt update && apt install -y nginx curl git
output:
Get:1 http://archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu jammy/main amd64 nginx amd64 1.18.0-6ubuntu1 [44.0 kB]
Fetched 44.0 kB in 1s (44.0 kB/s)
Selecting previously unselected package nginx.
Setting up nginx (1.18.0-6ubuntu1) ...
Processing triggers for systemd (249.11-0ubuntu3) ...
tip: Ubuntu releases follow YY.MM naming. LTS (Long Term Support) releases come every 2 years (20.04, 22.04, 24.04) — prefer these for servers.

title: Debian
description: The universal Linux OS. Upstream of Ubuntu, known for rock-solid stability. Runs on more hardware architectures than any other distro. Three branches: stable, testing, unstable.

breakdown.meaning: APT package handling utility (lower-level than apt)

example:
# Check Debian version
cat /etc/debian_version

# Install essentials
apt-get update && apt-get install -y sudo curl wget vim
output:
12.4

Reading package lists... Done
Building dependency tree... Done
0 upgraded, 4 newly installed, 0 to remove
Need to get 8,742 kB of archives.
Do you want to continue? [Y/n] y
tip: Debian stable is very conservative — packages may be 1-2 years behind upstream. Use backports (deb ... bookworm-backports) for newer versions of specific packages.

title: RHEL / CentOS Stream
description: Red Hat Enterprise Linux is the enterprise standard for production Linux. CentOS Stream is its freely available upstream. Uses RPM packages and dnf/yum. Dominates enterprise data centers.

breakdown.meaning: Dandified YUM — next-gen package manager for RHEL/Fedora

flags.description: Install RPM file with verbose output and progress

example:
# Enable EPEL repository then install packages
dnf install -y epel-release
dnf install -y htop ncdu jq
tip: RHEL uses SELinux in enforcing mode by default — many issues are SELinux-related. Check with 'ausearch -m avc' or 'sealert -a /var/log/audit/audit.log'.

title: Fedora
description: Red Hat's community cutting-edge distro. Features the very latest software — Fedora gets new packages 6-12 months before they reach RHEL. New release every 6 months with 13 months support.

breakdown.meaning: Dandified YUM — Fedora's primary package manager

flags.description: Refresh metadata and upgrade all packages

example:
# Add RPM Fusion repo (non-free software)
dnf install -y https://download1.rpmfusion.org/free/fedora/rpmfusion-free-release-$(rpm -E %fedora).noarch.rpm
dnf install -y vlc
output:
RPM Fusion for Fedora 39 - Free - 14 kB/s | 3.6 kB     00:00
Dependencies resolved.
...
Installed:
  vlc-3.0.20-3.fc39.x86_64
tip: Fedora Workstation is excellent for developers who want latest tools. Use 'dnf history undo' to roll back a bad update — a feature most distros lack.

title: Arch Linux
description: A rolling-release, minimalist distro built around simplicity and user control. You install exactly what you need. Legendary Arch Wiki is one of the best Linux documentation resources. Features the AUR (Arch User Repository) with 90,000+ packages.

flags.description: Sync, refresh db, and upgrade all packages
Remove package and its unused dependencies
Display detailed info about installed package
List all files owned by package
Find which package owns a file

example:
# System update
pacman -Syu

# Install with AUR helper (yay)
yay -S google-chrome
output:
:: Synchronizing package databases...
 core is up to date
 extra is up to date
:: Starting full system upgrade...
 resolving dependencies...
:: Proceed with installation? (Y/n) y
(142/142) checking keys in keyring        [######################] 100%
tip: Never do partial upgrades on Arch (pacman -Sy package without -u). Always run full -Syu to avoid dependency hell. Check news.archlinux.org before upgrading.

title: Alpine Linux
description: Ultra-minimal Linux distro designed for security and small footprint. Base image is only ~5MB. The standard base image for Docker containers. Uses musl libc instead of glibc and busybox instead of GNU coreutils.

breakdown.meaning: Alpine Package Keeper — Alpine's package manager

flags.description: Install without caching index (best for Docker layers)

example:
# Typical Alpine Dockerfile pattern
FROM alpine:3.19
RUN apk add --no-cache curl bash ca-certificates
output:
fetch https://dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org/alpine/v3.19/main/x86_64/APKINDEX.tar.gz
fetch https://dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org/alpine/v3.19/community/x86_64/APKINDEX.tar.gz
(1/3) Installing ca-certificates (20240226-r0)
(2/3) Installing curl (8.5.0-r0)
(3/3) Installing bash (5.2.21-r0)
OK: 12 MiB in 16 packages
tip: Use --no-cache in Dockerfiles to avoid storing the package index in the image layer, keeping images smaller. Note: some software compiled for glibc won't run on Alpine's musl libc.

title: Amazon Linux 2023
description: AWS's purpose-built Linux distro, optimized for EC2. AL2023 is based on Fedora/RHEL, uses DNF, and ships with AWS CLI pre-installed. Long-term support until 2028.
example:
# Check AL version and install common tools
cat /etc/system-release
dnf install -y git htop tmux aws-cli
output:
Amazon Linux 2023

Dependencies resolved.
 Package     Arch    Version          Repository  Size
 Installing:
 git         x86_64  2.40.1-1.amzn2023  amazonlinux 6.3 M
 htop        x86_64  3.2.1-1.amzn2023   amazonlinux 290 k
Installed: git-2.40.1, htop-3.2.1, tmux-3.3a, aws-cli-2.x
tip: AL2023 dropped support for amazon-linux-extras. If you're upgrading from AL2, many extras are now standard packages in AL2023 repos.

title: openSUSE
description: German-engineered, enterprise-grade Linux. Two flavors: Leap (stable, point release, based on SUSE Enterprise) and Tumbleweed (rolling release). Features YaST — the most comprehensive Linux system administration tool.
example:
# Tumbleweed full upgrade
zypper refresh && zypper dup
output:

Loading repository data...

tip: openSUSE Tumbleweed is arguably the best rolling-release distro for stability — it uses automated testing to prevent regressions before packages hit users.

title: Kali Linux
description: Debian-based distro specialized for penetration testing and security auditing. Ships with 600+ pre-installed security tools. Maintained by Offensive Security. Runs as root by default since Kali 2020.

breakdown.meaning: Kali uses Debian's APT package manager
Package or security tool to install

flags.description: Install web application security tools only

example:
# Update Kali and install a specific tool
apt update && apt install -y gobuster
gobuster --version
output:
Get:1 http://http.kali.org/kali kali-rolling/main amd64 gobuster amd64 3.6.0-0kali1 [2,453 kB]
Fetched 2,453 kB in 2s (1,226 kB/s)
Setting up gobuster (3.6.0-0kali1) ...

gobuster v3.6.0
tip: Kali is for security testing, not daily use. Use it in a VM or live boot for pentesting engagements. Install only the tool categories you need — 'everything' is 15+ GB.

title: NixOS
description: Declarative, reproducible Linux distro. The entire system — packages, services, users, configs — is defined in a single /etc/nixos/configuration.nix file. Atomic upgrades with instant rollback to any previous generation.

breakdown.meaning: Nix environment manager for managing packages
Package attribute path in the Nixpkgs collection

flags.description: Open a temporary shell with package available

output:
building the system configuration...
activating the configuration...
restarting the following units: nginx.service

# Generation 42 created — rollback with:
# nixos-rebuild switch --rollback
tip: Use 'nix-shell -p nodejs python3 postgresql' for ephemeral dev environments that disappear when you exit — perfect for project-specific tooling without polluting the system.

title: Rocky Linux / AlmaLinux
description: 1:1 binary-compatible RHEL rebuilds, created after CentOS 8 was discontinued. Rocky Linux (by one of CentOS's original founders) and AlmaLinux (by CloudLinux) are the primary CentOS replacements for production servers.

breakdown.meaning: DNF package manager — identical to RHEL's

flags.description: Enable EPEL repository for extra packages
Enable a specific module stream version
Register with Red Hat (RHEL only, not needed for Rocky/Alma)

example:
cat /etc/rocky-release
dnf install -y epel-release
dnf install -y htop tmux git
output:
Rocky Linux release 9.3 (Blue Onyx)

Dependencies resolved.
 Package      Arch    Version     Repository  Size
 Installing:
 epel-release noarch  9-5.el9     extras      18 k

Installed:
  epel-release-9-5.el9.noarch
tip: Rocky and Alma are drop-in CentOS 8 replacements. If you have existing RHEL/CentOS configs and RPM specs, they should work without modification.

title: Distribution upgrades and tips
description: Key operations that apply across Debian/Ubuntu family distros: release upgrades, PPA management, and package pinning.

breakdown.meaning: Ubuntu/Debian tool to upgrade to the next OS release

flags.description: Add a PPA (Personal Package Archive) repository
Prevent a package from being upgraded
Allow a held package to upgrade again
Show available versions and which repo they come from
List all packages with their state

example:
# Hold a specific package version
apt-mark hold nginx
nginx set on hold.

# Check which repos provide a package
apt-cache policy nginx
output:
nginx:
  Installed: 1.18.0-6ubuntu1
  Candidate: 1.24.0-1~jammy
  Version table:
 *** 1.18.0-6ubuntu1 500
        500 http://archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu jammy/main amd64 Packages
     1.24.0-1~jammy 500
        500 http://ppa.launchpadcontent.net/ondrej/nginx/ubuntu jammy/main
tip: Use apt-mark hold to pin critical packages (kernel, nginx) before major upgrades. Always test do-release-upgrade in a VM or snapshot first.
